title.narrative: HAY Mining, Health and Communications Project

description.narrative:
Despite the fact the Yanomami people were granted the right to their territory in 1992, illegal gold miners continue to enter their territory, creating violence, disease, and polluting rivers from mercury used in the extraction of gold. In addition, quality health services in indigenous communities are in crisis in Brazil – many lack medicines, drinking water and transport for patients to reach health services in their communities, and only 2.2 per cent of communities are connected to a sewerage system. The infant mortality rate in indigenous communities is double the rest of the country’s population.
Therefore, the main objective of this project is to protect Yanomami and Ye’kuana communities against illegal gold mining, and increase their access to quality health services through the improvement of communications and information sharing between HAY and three vulnerable communities in TIY.
Key activities include: (i) installing three radios in three communities in TIY that are particularly vulnerable to mining threats and health problems; (ii) training communities on how to use and maintain the radios as a form of constant communication with HAY on threats; (iii) publish 2 bi-annual newsletters on mining and health in Portuguese and Yanomami to raise awareness of indigenous rights and threats posed to indigenous communities; (v) publish 2 public reports on mining threats and health problems and service deficiencies in TIY, (vi) lobby for and accompany the process of removing illegal invaders, and the implementation of permanent inspection of lands by governmental authorities, including FUNAI; and (vii) update their website: http://hutukara.org/ with news articles on progress of HAY’s work.
